events.title: Cathode-Ray Tube Amusement Device Patented
events.description: Thomas T. Goldsmith Jr. and Estle Ray Mann patent the first interactive electronic game, a missile simulator using a cathode-ray tube.

events.title: Nimrod Computer Unveiled
events.description: The Nimrod computer, designed specifically to play the game of Nim, is displayed at the Festival of Britain.

events.title: OXO (Noughts and Crosses) Created
events.description: Alexander S. Douglas creates one of the first games in the history of computing, a version of Tic-Tac-Toe for the EDSAC computer.

events.title: Tennis for Two Demonstrated
events.description: Physicist William Higinbotham creates an interactive game called Tennis for Two on an oscilloscope for an open house at Brookhaven National Laboratory.

events.title: Spacewar! Developed at MIT
events.description: Steve Russell and a team at MIT develop Spacewar!, one of the first digital computer games, on the DEC PDP-1.

events.title: The 'Brown Box' Prototype
events.description: Ralph Baer and his team at Sanders Associates develop the 'Brown Box', the first prototype for a multi-program, multi-player video game system.

events.title: Computer Space Released
events.description: Nolan Bushnell and Ted Dabney release Computer Space, the first commercially sold coin-operated video game.

events.title: Magnavox Odyssey Launch
events.description: The Magnavox Odyssey, the first commercial home video game console, is released.

events.title: Pong Released by Atari
events.description: Atari releases Pong, the first commercially successful arcade video game, sparking the arcade revolution.

events.title: Space Race Released
events.description: Atari's second game, Space Race, becomes the first racing video game.

events.title: Gran Trak 10 Released
events.description: Atari releases Gran Trak 10, the first arcade racing game with a steering wheel and pedals.

events.title: Gun Fight Released
events.description: Midway releases Gun Fight, the first video game to use a microprocessor (Intel 8080).

events.title: Breakout Released
events.description: Atari releases Breakout, conceptualized by Nolan Bushnell and Steve Bristow, and influenced by Apple co-founders Steve Jobs and Steve Wozniak.

events.title: Fairchild Channel F Launch
events.description: The Fairchild Channel F is released, the first console to use programmable ROM cartridges.

events.title: Atari 2600 (VCS) Launch
events.description: Atari releases the Video Computer System (later renamed Atari 2600), bringing cartridge-based gaming to the masses.

events.title: Space Invaders Released
events.description: Taito releases Space Invaders in Japan, a massive success that defines the 'Shoot 'em up' genre.

events.title: Magnavox Odyssey 2 Launch
events.description: The Odyssey 2 is released, featuring a full alphanumeric keyboard.

events.title: Activision Founded
events.description: Four former Atari programmers found Activision, the world's first independent third-party video game developer.

events.title: Asteroids Released
events.description: Atari releases Asteroids, which becomes their best-selling arcade game of all time.

events.title: Galaxian Released
events.description: Namco releases Galaxian, the first game with 100% RGB color graphics.

events.title: Game & Watch Launch
events.description: Nintendo releases the Game & Watch series, created by Gunpei Yokoi, the first successful line of handheld electronic games.

events.title: Pac-Man Released
events.description: Namco releases Pac-Man (originally Puckman in Japan), which becomes a global cultural phenomenon.

events.title: Donkey Kong Released
events.description: Nintendo releases Donkey Kong, introducing the world to Jumpman (later Mario) and Pauline.

events.title: Galaga Released
events.description: Namco releases Galaga, a hugely popular sequel to Galaxian.

events.title: Ms. Pac-Man Released
events.description: Midway releases Ms. Pac-Man, which many consider an improvement over the original.

events.title: Pitfall! Released
events.description: Activision releases Pitfall!, a landmark title for the Atari 2600 that defines the side-scrolling platformer.

events.title: E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial Released
events.description: Atari releases E.T., widely considered one of the worst games ever and a major factor in the 1983 crash.

events.title: The Video Game Crash of 1983
events.description: A massive recession in the North American video game industry occurs due to market saturation and low-quality games.

events.title: Dragon's Lair Released
events.description: Cinematronics releases Dragon's Lair, the first major LaserDisc arcade game, featuring animation by Don Bluth.

events.title: Nintendo Entertainment System (Famicom) Launch in Japan
events.description: Nintendo releases the Family Computer (Famicom) in Japan, which would later be redesigned as the NES.

events.title: Tetris Created
events.description: Alexey Pajitnov creates Tetris on an Electronika 60 while working for the Soviet Academy of Sciences.

events.title: Super Mario Bros. Released
events.description: Nintendo releases Super Mario Bros. for the Famicom, a game that revitalizes the industry after the crash.

events.title: NES Launch in North America
events.description: The Nintendo Entertainment System is test-launched in New York City, marking Nintendo's entry into the US market.

events.title: The Legend of Zelda Released
events.description: Nintendo releases The Legend of Zelda in Japan, introducing save batteries and non-linear open-world exploration.

events.title: Metroid Released
events.description: Nintendo releases Metroid, featuring Samus Aran, one of the first prominent female protagonists in gaming.

events.title: Sega Master System Launch in North America
events.description: The Sega Master System is released in the US to compete with the NES.

events.title: Mega Man Released
events.description: Capcom releases Mega Man (Rockman) for the NES, starting a long-running franchise.

events.title: Final Fantasy Released
events.description: Square releases Final Fantasy for the NES, a last-ditch effort that becomes a massive success and saves the company.

events.title: Sega Genesis (Mega Drive) Launch in Japan
events.description: Sega releases the 16-bit Mega Drive in Japan, later known as the Genesis in North America.

events.title: Game Boy Launch
events.description: Nintendo releases the Game Boy, which becomes the most successful handheld console of its time, bundled with Tetris.

events.title: SimCity Released
events.description: Maxis releases Will Wright's SimCity, a game that defines the city-building simulation genre.

events.title: Super Nintendo Entertainment System (Super Famicom) Launch
events.description: Nintendo releases the Super Famicom in Japan, continuing its dominance into the 16-bit era.

events.title: Street Fighter II Released
events.description: Capcom releases Street Fighter II in arcades, sparking a massive fighting game craze.

events.title: Sonic the Hedgehog Released
events.description: Sega releases Sonic the Hedgehog, giving them a mascot to compete with Mario and boosting Genesis sales.

events.title: Wolfenstein 3D Released
events.description: id Software releases Wolfenstein 3D, widely considered the 'grandfather' of the first-person shooter genre.

events.title: Mortal Kombat Released
events.description: Midway releases Mortal Kombat, notorious for its realistic digitized graphics and 'Fatalities', leading to the creation of the ESRB.

events.title: Myst Released
events.description: Cyan releases Myst, which becomes the best-selling PC game of the 90s and pushes CD-ROM adoption.

events.title: Doom Released
events.description: id Software releases Doom, a landmark FPS that popularizes networked multiplayer and 3D graphics.

events.title: Sega Saturn Launch in Japan
events.description: Sega releases the Saturn, a powerful 2D machine that struggled against the PlayStation in 3D performance.

events.title: PlayStation Launch in Japan
events.description: Sony releases the PlayStation, marking their successful entry into the console market after a failed deal with Nintendo.

events.title: Wipeout Released
events.description: Psygnosis releases Wipeout for the PlayStation, featuring a cool electronic soundtrack that appeals to adult club culture.

events.title: Pokémon Red and Blue Released in Japan
events.description: Nintendo releases Pokémon Red and Green (later Blue) for the Game Boy, starting a global phenomenon.

events.title: Quake Released
events.description: id Software releases Quake, featuring a true 3D engine and pioneering online multiplayer via QuakeWorld.

events.title: Super Mario 64 Released
events.description: Nintendo releases Super Mario 64, which sets the standard for 3D platformers and camera control.

events.title: Nintendo 64 Launch
events.description: Nintendo releases the N64, their first console capable of high-fidelity 3D graphics, but sticking to cartridges.

events.title: Tomb Raider Released
events.description: Core Design releases Tomb Raider, introducing the iconic Lara Croft.

events.title: Final Fantasy VII Released
events.description: Square releases Final Fantasy VII on the PlayStation, bringing the JRPG genre to the mainstream in the West.

events.title: GoldenEye 007 Released
events.description: Rare releases GoldenEye 007 for the N64, proving that FPS games can work on consoles and have great multiplayer.

events.title: StarCraft Released
events.description: Blizzard releases StarCraft, which becomes a cornerstone of competitive RTS gaming and eSports in South Korea.

events.title: Metal Gear Solid Released
events.description: Konami releases Metal Gear Solid, a cinematic stealth-action game directed by Hideo Kojima.

events.title: Half-Life Released
events.description: Valve releases Half-Life, revolutionizing storytelling in FPS games without the use of cutscenes.

events.title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Released
events.description: Nintendo releases Ocarina of Time, often cited as one of the greatest games ever made, pioneering Z-targeting.

events.title: Dreamcast Launch in Japan
events.description: Sega releases the Dreamcast, their final console, featuring a built-in modem for online play.

events.title: EverQuest Released
events.description: Verant Interactive and 989 Studios release EverQuest, a highly influential MMORPG.

events.title: Counter-Strike Released as a Mod
events.description: Minh Le and Jess Cliffe release the first beta of Counter-Strike, a mod for Half-Life that becomes the most popular online shooter.

events.title: The Sims Released
events.description: Maxis releases The Sims, which becomes a massive crossover hit and one of the best-selling PC games of all time.

events.title: PlayStation 2 Launch in Japan
events.description: Sony releases the PS2, which becomes the best-selling home console of all time, doubling as a DVD player.

events.title: GameCube Launch in Japan
events.description: Nintendo releases the GameCube, their first console to use optical discs (mini-DVDs).

events.title: Grand Theft Auto III Released
events.description: Rockstar North releases GTA III, revolutionizing the open-world 'sandbox' genre in 3D.

events.title: Halo: Combat Evolved Released
events.description: Microsoft releases Halo as a launch title for the Xbox, defining the console FPS for a new generation.

events.title: Xbox Launch
events.description: Microsoft enters the console market with the Xbox, featuring a built-in hard drive and Ethernet port.

events.title: Steam Launched
events.description: Valve launches Steam as a platform for game updates and digital distribution, eventually dominating the PC market.

events.title: Nintendo DS Launch
events.description: Nintendo releases the DS, featuring dual screens and a touch interface, starting a new era of handheld gaming.

events.title: World of Warcraft Released
events.description: Blizzard releases WoW, which becomes the most popular subscription-based MMORPG in history.

events.title: PlayStation Portable (PSP) Launch
events.description: Sony releases the PSP, their first foray into handhelds, featuring impressive graphics and a UMD drive.

events.title: Guitar Hero Released
events.description: Harmonix releases Guitar Hero, sparking a rhythm game boom with its plastic guitar controller.

events.title: Xbox 360 Launch
events.description: Microsoft releases the Xbox 360, ushering in the HD era and popularizing digital achievements.

events.title: PlayStation 3 Launch
events.description: Sony releases the PS3, featuring a Blu-ray drive and the Cell processor.

events.title: Wii Launch
events.description: Nintendo releases the Wii, featuring motion controls that appeal to a wide 'casual' audience.

events.title: iPhone Launch
events.description: Apple releases the iPhone, which would soon revolutionize mobile gaming with the App Store.

events.title: BioShock Released
events.description: 2K Games releases BioShock, a critically acclaimed 'immersive sim' with a deep philosophical narrative.

events.title: Call of Duty 4: Modern Warfare Released
events.description: Activision releases Modern Warfare, which redefines the military shooter and sets new standards for online multiplayer.

events.title: Grand Theft Auto IV Released
events.description: Rockstar releases GTA IV, a more grounded and realistic take on the open-world series.

events.title: Minecraft (Alpha) Released
events.description: Markus 'Notch' Persson releases the first public version of Minecraft, which becomes a global phenomenon and the best-selling game ever.

events.title: League of Legends Released
events.description: Riot Games releases League of Legends, which becomes a dominant force in the MOBA genre and global eSports.

events.title: Angry Birds Released
events.description: Rovio releases Angry Birds on iOS, proving the massive potential of simple touch-based mobile games.

events.title: Twitch.tv Founded
events.description: Justin.tv launches Twitch as a spin-off for gaming content, revolutionizing how people watch and stream games.

events.title: Dark Souls Released
events.description: FromSoftware releases Dark Souls, known for its high difficulty and deep lore, spawning the 'Soulslike' genre.

events.title: The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim Released
events.description: Bethesda releases Skyrim, an open-world RPG that becomes a massive cultural hit and meme source.

events.title: Candy Crush Saga Released on Mobile
events.description: King releases Candy Crush Saga on mobile, popularizing the 'freemium' match-three puzzle game.

events.title: Wii U Launch
events.description: Nintendo releases the Wii U, featuring a tablet-like GamePad, which struggled to find a market.

events.title: Grand Theft Auto V Released
events.description: Rockstar releases GTA V, one of the most profitable entertainment products ever, featuring three playable protagonists.

events.title: PlayStation 4 Launch
events.description: Sony releases the PS4, focusing on a gamer-first approach and social sharing.

events.title: Xbox One Launch
events.description: Microsoft releases the Xbox One, initially marketed as an all-in-one entertainment system.

events.title: Oculus Rift Launch
events.description: The first consumer version of the Oculus Rift is released, bringing high-end VR to the consumer market.

events.title: Overwatch Released
events.description: Blizzard releases Overwatch, a popular 'hero shooter' that becomes a major eSports title.

events.title: Pokémon GO Released
events.description: Niantic and Nintendo release Pokémon GO, a massive AR mobile hit that encourages people to explore the real world.

events.title: The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild Released
events.description: Nintendo releases Breath of the Wild, a revolutionary open-world game that breaks many series conventions.

events.title: Nintendo Switch Launch
events.description: Nintendo releases the Switch, a hybrid console that can be played both on a TV and in handheld mode.

events.title: Fortnite Battle Royale Released
events.description: Epic Games releases the Battle Royale mode for Fortnite, which becomes a global cultural phenomenon and crossover powerhouse.

events.title: Animal Crossing: New Horizons Released
events.description: Nintendo releases New Horizons during the global pandemic, becoming a vital social tool for millions.

events.title: Xbox Series X and S Launch
events.description: Microsoft releases their next-gen consoles, focusing on Game Pass and backward compatibility.

events.title: PlayStation 5 Launch
events.description: Sony releases the PS5, featuring a high-speed SSD and the DualSense controller.

events.title: Elden Ring Released
events.description: FromSoftware releases Elden Ring, an open-world evolution of the Souls formula that becomes a massive critical and commercial hit.

events.title: Steam Deck Launch
events.description: Valve releases the Steam Deck, a powerful handheld PC that redefines portable gaming for the PC market.
